# Token discipline

Distilled from the source repo's `web-store-tokens` skill — the parts that don't depend on the source repo's own file paths.

## The one scanner limitation to respect

The guardrail's token check is a regex over your CSS text — it cannot see through a token name built via string interpolation:

```js
// INVISIBLE to the guardrail — never do this:
const style = { background: `var(--x-bg-action-${variant})` }
```

```js
// Correct — a literal lookup object, so every possible token name appears
// as plain text somewhere in your source:
const BG = {
  primary: 'var(--x-bg-action-primary)',
  secondary: 'var(--x-bg-action-secondary)',
}
const style = { background: BG[variant] }
```

## Container queries, never viewport media queries

This component library has no `@media`-based responsive system — every component reflows via CSS container queries (`@container`). If you add layout CSS that needs to respond to width, wrap it in a container (`container-type: inline-size` on a parent) and use `@container (min-width: …)`, never `@media (min-width: …)`.

### Source: `web-store-tokens` — "2. THE RULE — what a component may consume"

**Components consume ONLY:**
- the **semantic colour** tier — `--x-bg-*`, `--x-text-*`, `--x-border-*`
- the **semantic spacing** tier — `--x-pad-*`, `--x-gap-*`, `--x-radius-*`, `--x-size-*`, `--x-border-weight-*`
- the **`.text-style-*`** classes (never raw `font-size`/`font-weight`/`line-height`/`letter-spacing`)
- **`extensions.css`** tokens for brand effects with no semantic slot

> Every real token in this repo carries an **`--x-` prefix** (`--x-bg-*`, `--x-sys-colour-*`,
> `--x-palette-*`, `--x-ref-*`, …) — confirmed by reading `semantics.css`/`system.css`/any
> `themes/*.css`. Any rule, grep gate, or code example in this skill (or `codm-web-store-fe`)
> that omits the `x-` must be read as shorthand for the prefixed name — but if you're pasting a
> grep command from either skill, paste it **with** the `--x-` prefix or it will silently match
> nothing. This exact gap — a grep gate checking `--(bg|text|border)-` instead of
> `--x-(bg|text|border)-` — let 7 tier-skip violations across 6 store theme files ship undetected
> (see `zzz.css`/`diabloimmortal.css`/`mcoc.css`/`codashop.css`/`ygodl.css`/`ygomd.css` history).
> **Verify every grep gate actually matches a token that exists in the repo before trusting an
> empty result — an empty result from a mistyped pattern looks identical to a clean sweep.**

**NEVER in a component:**
- a raw literal — `#hex`, `rgba()`, `oklch()`, `linear-gradient(<brand colour>)`, bare `1px`/`2px`,
  raw `px` font-size — **except** `var(--x-token, <fallback>)` and CSS **mask idioms** (`linear-gradient(#fff 0 0)`
  / `#000` used purely as mask alpha, not brand colour)
- a **system / spectrum / seed** token directly — `--x-sys-colour-*`, `--x-palette-*`, `--x-ref-*` (upstream structure)
- a **legacy ad-hoc name** (these were removed — see the rename cheat-sheet in `codm-web-store-fe` §1)

Why: a component that only reads the semantic tier is automatically reskinnable — every store
retargets the semantic token in its theme block and the component never changes.

### Source: `web-store-tokens` — "2b. The semantic set is closed — stop and ask, don't extend it"

**While building or editing a component, the semantic tiers are a closed set:**
`--x-bg-*`, `--x-text-*`, `--x-border-*`, `--x-pad-*`, `--x-gap-*`, `--x-radius-*`,
`--x-size-*`, `--x-border-weight-*`, and the `.text-style-*` classes. You **pick**
from this set; you never **extend** it mid-component. A new semantic token is a
design decision — it belongs to the person who owns the design system, not to
whoever happens to be implementing a component that day.

This does **not** apply to `extensions.css` brand effects or `material-fx`'s
`--x-material-*`/`--x-light-*` axes — a genuinely new visual effect (shimmer, comet
border, glass, a rarity fill) can still get a new token there, per §4 below. The
closed-set rule is specifically the semantic colour/space/type tiers.

**Before writing any component CSS, enumerate what already exists** — don't guess a
token name and check it after:

```bash
grep -oE -- "--x-(bg|text|border|pad|gap|radius|size|border-weight)-[a-z0-9-]+" \
  src/tokens/ds/semantics.css src/tokens/ds/space.css | sort -u
```

**If nothing in that list fits, stop — do not reach for the nearest token and keep
going, and do not add a new one yourself.** Surface a short report instead:

1. What the component needs (the visual/spacing/type role, in plain terms).
2. The closest 1–3 existing tokens and what they actually resolve to.
3. Why each one falls short (off by how much, or the wrong role entirely).
4. The options: reuse one of them anyway · retune it · add a new token (name the
   tier it would live in) — **the user decides; do not add it yourself.**

Only once the user has chosen "add a new token" does §4's "Adding a token — which
tier?" mechanics apply — those steps describe *how*, this rule decides *whether*,
and for a component change that decision is the user's.

**Self-check before calling a component done**: `git diff src/tokens/ds/semantics.css
src/tokens/ds/space.css src/tokens/ds/text-styles.css` must be **empty**. Any
addition there during what was meant to be a component-only change means a new
semantic token slipped in without the stop-and-ask gate running.
